Weather & Weekend Rundown:

Find the warm coat, because this weekend swings from soggy to wintry to gorgeous in three days. Friday is wet and windy, with rain heavy at times, a break around mid morning, then more showers along a cold front this afternoon and early evening, a high near 60 and south gusts around 40 mph in the Champlain Valley that could bring down a few branches. The showers end this evening as the wind turns northwest, and tonight drops to the mid 30s while the mountains turn to snow. Saturday is the coldest day of the season so far, with highs only around 40, northwest gusts near 30 mph and morning wind chills in the 20s, and a few stray flakes could even mix in down here in the morning before the sun comes out in the afternoon. Saturday night drops right to freezing, then Sunday turns sunny with a high in the mid 50s, and Monday is sunny and near 60 to start a long dry stretch. Track it all week, with patio, swim, and sunset scores, at Burlington Right Now.

Friday

  • Champlain Valley Craft Show & Antique Expo – Fri through Sun from 10: More than 125 artisan booths plus a curated antique expo fill the Champlain Valley Expo, with live craft demos all weekend. One $12 admission covers all three days, and kids under 14 get in free.

  • BCA Fall Exhibitions Opening – 5 to 7 PM: BCA celebrates three new shows, Dark Botanica, Kathleen Schneider and Trystan Bates, with drinks and light refreshments at the BCA Center on Church Street. Vermont teachers get their own social hour with the exhibition artists at 4.

  • ECHO After Dark: Memento Mori – 6 PM: ECHO goes 18+ for a night of death and decomposition science from real experts, a danse macabre ball and a costume contest with a Best in Theme category for Death and Decay ($30).

  • Spirits of Rokeby – Fri & Sat evenings: Down in Ferrisburgh, Rokeby Museum recreates séances from its own records inside the historic home, after a drink and a short talk on Victorian Spiritualism. Slots hold 15 and sell in advance ($25).

  • The S-Creemee Dreemee Puppet Slam – 7 PM: Junktiques hosts an evening of puppetry for adults from local artists and traveling puppeteers, with acts that may be funny, quirky, dark or even profound ($10 to $20 sliding scale).

  • VTIFF Opening Night – 7 PM: The 10 day film festival opens at Main Street Landing with a 9 PM party, then runs through Oct. 25 ($12, $6 students). Its opening film, Palme d'Or winner Fjord, is currently full.

  • Sex With Jenna – Doors 7:30: Sexuality educator and comedian Jenna Emerson hosts a live Dating Game style show at Higher Ground where you can watch or play for a sponsored first date, then DJ Gay Bar takes over for a dance party (18+).

Also Friday, DBVI and VABVI lead a quarter mile White Cane Awareness Day walk from 200 Pearl Street to City Hall at 10, honoring Anne Connelly, who brought Vermont its first trained guide dog in 1930, and UVM professor Alex Zakaras gives the EEE talk Freedom for All, What a Liberal Society Could Be at Faith United Methodist Church in South Burlington at 2. Early evening brings Radio Cowboy to Switchback's beer garden at 5:30 and a free honky tonk set from Danny & The Parts at Shelburne Vineyard at 6, while Queen City Cat Lounge hosts Crochet with Cats, where you learn to make a catnip toy while you hang out with cats waiting for adoption, and the Richard Kemp Center has a family friendly game night, both at 6. Hometown comic Kendall Farrell headlines the Vermont Comedy Club at 6:30, with two more shows Saturday.

At 7, Déjà Rêvé's 'Venus in Fur' plays its last weekend at Off Center for the Dramatic Arts (closing Saturday), Vermont Rep's Williston One Acts stage short plays by Elaine May, Harold Pinter and Richard Greenberg, and NBT Bank opens The Bank Backrooms, a free liminal space haunted house benefiting Steps to End Domestic Violence, until 9. Lizzie Murderz hosts the Geeky & Freaky edition of Supernova drag and burlesque at Standing Stone in Winooski (doors at 7), Higher Ground has Burlington's Led Zeppelin tribute Nico Suave & The Mothership (doors at 7, tickets running low), and EDM fans can catch Blood Eclipse and five more acts at Odd Fellows Hall at 7 ($10). Later, Moonbird plays The Old Post at 8 and DJ Taka spins at Standing Stone at 11.

Saturday

  • BTown Coffee Club [MEETUP] – 10 AM: Our weekly coffee and conversation at Zero Gravity, so come warm up with us.

  • PokeKon-Fest – 10 to 5: An all Pokémon show at the DoubleTree in South Burlington, with vendors selling cards, toys, video games, retro finds, artwork and apparel, plus voice actors ($20, kids under 11 free).

  • Ryan Hagen: Your Guide to Climate Action – 11 AM: For anyone worried or angry about climate breakdown who wants to do something about it, the author talks at the South Burlington library, with signed copies for sale and a giveaway.

  • Flaxtravaganza – 11 to 2: The Ethan Allen Homestead celebrates the end of flax season with reenactors in the Allen House, a costume corner and how people made fiber from their own gardens to protest British made cloth. Free, and the last reenactment of 2026.

  • Zombie Walk – 4 PM: The undead gather on the Church Street side of City Hall by 3:30, then stumble up and down Church Street in search of brains until 4:30. Free and family friendly.

  • Borderlands – Sat & Sun evenings: Small groups set out every fifteen minutes at Shelburne Farms ($25, $15 kids), and Friday's shows are cancelled for the rain. Treewild's walk through an illuminated forest has actors narrating while the audience acts out Calypso and Odysseus with shadow puppets.

  • Bob the Drag Queen: Now Clap! – 6 PM: The Drag Race winner, Broadway star and best selling author brings the tour to the Flynn's Main Stage.

  • Judge – Doors 7: Higher Ground throws Gary Lane's 60th birthday with legendary New York hardcore band Judge, Vermont vets Get a Grip and a covers set of Gary's favorites by longtime friends. Tickets are running low.

Also Saturday, the Burlington Farmers Market runs 9 to 2 on Pine Street rain or shine, where Aging in Place with Pets tables most Saturdays, and the Shelburne Farmers Market holds its last market of the season on the Parade Grounds from 9 to 1, with live music at 10. Check in opens at 9 for the Out of the Darkness Walk at Veterans Memorial Park, a walk of 1 to 3 miles to prevent suicide that's free to register, Brownell Library in Essex Junction runs a free Halloween costume swap from 9 to 4:30 while supplies last, and Vermont Comedy Arts holds its free improv drop-in for all levels at the Vermont Comedy Club at 10. Lab B's Old North End Repair Cafe runs 11 to 3, where anyone can have anything repaired for free, and historian Richard Allen talks Taverns and Stagecoaches of Chittenden County at the Dorothy Alling library in Williston at 11:30.

In the afternoon, Essex Junction's Early Voting Jamboree walks, rides and rolls from Maple Street Park to the ballot boxes at 2:30 (bring a sign, a decorated bike or a noisemaker), VTIFF screens Lukas Dhont's World War I love story 'Coward' at the Film House at 4, and Sk802 hosts an intro to wild ice skating at Fletcher Free Library at 4 with a social after at Wallflower Collective. From 5, Passion 4 Paws throws a Nashville country concert with Jamie Lee Thurston and Hayley Sue on Jericho Road in Essex Junction for rescue dogs, and at 6 Girls on the Run Vermont throws its Sneaker Soirée at the Essex Resort with DJ Mega Luna and a silent auction ($75). The night also has Burning Roses Burlesque's Hex Appeal at Einstein's (21+, doors at 7), Los Songoros playing Latin music at the Venetian at 7, metal band Executive Disorder with Psychomanteum at Odd Fellows Hall at 7, and Baby Fearn's special and spooky free show at Foam at 8.

Sunday

  • Miller Symposium – 9 to 6:30: UVM's tenth Miller Symposium, The German Army and the Holocaust, runs free at the Alumni House, with talks on how the Wehrmacht became a genocidal army, its chaplains and the Nuremberg trials of its high command.

  • The Grave Side of Halloween – 10:30 AM: Dr. Elise Guyette leads an Elmwood Cemetery tour, then it's on to the ONE Community Center for a light luncheon, music by Woody Woodhead, a talk on iron grave markers and a raffle with prizes like a juggling lesson. Free, with donations to the Burlington History & Culture Center.

  • Winooski Vintage Market – 11 AM: Local sellers bring vintage clothing, accessories and home goods to Four Quarters Brewing at 70 Main St in Winooski from 11 to 6, so come shop and grab a beer while you're there.

  • Burlington VT Wedding Show – 12 PM: Couples planning a wedding can meet wedding vendors, sample cakes, enjoy the entertainment and find wedding deals at the DoubleTree on Williston Road from 12 to 3 ($16.05 online, $15 at the door).

  • Wild Culture Fermentation Festival – 12 PM: Barr Hill's Montpelier distillery throws its third annual celebration of natural fermentation from 12 to 4, with Vermont vendors like Eden Cider, VT Cider Lab, Woodlawn Creamery and Umamiso bringing samples and goods. There's a kraut making demo at 1, a cider apple tasting at 2, free distillery tours with a mini honey and live music all afternoon ($8 advance, $10 door).

  • Champlain Valley Buddy Walk – 1 PM: The 16th annual walk for the Champlain Valley Down Syndrome Group steps off from Veterans Memorial Park, one of 250 Buddy Walks across the country this fall ($10, $40 family max).

  • Story Songs of the 70s – 4 PM: Tom DiMenna and a second artist play Gordon Lightfoot, Cat Stevens and Harry Chapin, songs like Sundown, Wild World and W.O.L.D., at the Cathedral Church of St. Paul.

  • Fright by Flashlight – 6 PM: Thea Lewis leads a Queen City Ghostwalk through Lakeview Cemetery with vintage ghost hunting tools ($25).

Also Sunday, Winooski Rec needs volunteer weeders to pull knotweed at Memorial Park from 10 to 12:30, with tools, gloves and snacks provided, and the Spirit of Ethan Allen sails narrated scenic cruises at 12, 2 and 4 before its season ends next Friday. Jeff & Gina play a free mix of R&B, rock, funk and jazz at Foam at 1, Norwich historian Zachary Bennett gives a free talk on Water, Power, and Revolution on the Winooski River at the Ethan Allen Homestead at 2, Higher Ground's Good Time Line Dancing opens doors at 7 for lessons and social dancing (tickets running low), and Karaoke Sundays close out the weekend at Einstein's from 9 (21+).

Local News (All Links Clickable)

New plans could bring Burlington’s Nectar’s back to life

"It’s very exciting news. You know, I’ve long thought that the closing of Nectar’s was one of the big reasons that this stretch of town was so barren for a while," per WCAX.

The Main Street club has been closed since last year, and Shawn Cliche has submitted a zoning application to use all three floors for food, live music, DJs and pool tables, day and night. He says it's still undecided whether the Nectar's name stays, and there's a long process ahead before music returns. Cliche has opened about 30 bars and clubs over the years, including a similar venue in Plattsburgh.

Yên Vietnamese Café & Kitchen to Launch Soon in Winooski

"It means the sense of peace and comfort that you feel on the inside," per Seven Days.

Summer Cao, 27, moved Donwoori Korean restaurant to 22 Main Street by the Winooski rotary and kept the lease on its old home at 65 Winooski Falls Way, where she expects to open Yên by the end of October. The 35 seat restaurant honors her late father with pho, fresh summer rolls, sticky fish sauce chicken wings and Vietnamese coffee made with robusta beans, plus mocktails and cocktails, for lunch and dinner six days a week.

Burlington mayor signs executive order on ICE enforcement; DHS pushes back

"This is nothing more than a political stunt by Vermont sanctuary politicians," per NBC5.

Mayor Emma Mulvaney-Stanak's order, signed Wednesday, lays out how Burlington will carry out Act 150, the state law in effect since June that restricts civil arrests, including immigration arrests, at schools, churches, libraries, hospitals, polling places and other designated locations. The city will update its signs, train employees on responding to federal immigration enforcement and work with legal organizations to help residents understand their rights, and Burlington police will not assist with civil immigration enforcement. DHS says ICE isn't targeting hospitals, schools or churches and isn't planning operations at polling places.

ICE is more active in Vermont. But federal data overstates it

"So ICE does appear to be on track to increase its interior arrests in Vermont this year, even if not as dramatically as the federal data suggests," per Vermont Public.

Widely cited federal data shows ICE logging 124 arrests in Vermont through July, more than triple all of 2025, but Vermont Public found more than 50 of those people closely match border crossers caught by Border Patrol and later handed to ICE, so their arrests were counted twice. ICE made 29 at large arrests in that stretch, including the March 11 detentions of three immigrants at their South Burlington home, compared with 35 in all of 2025. Since that data was compiled, Seven Days has identified at least 12 construction workers detained by ICE in August and early September.

‘Fuck the Flock cameras’: On big tech, Vermont’s candidates for governor differ on style and substance

"I think what you’re seeing here is an issue that really gets to the heart of the different governing philosophies between the two," per VTDigger.

Democratic nominee Amanda Janoo wants to ban Flock Safety's license plate reading cameras, which some Vermont police departments use, and to tell large data center companies they aren't welcome here for now, after Gov. Phil Scott vetoed a bill this year that would have regulated where they could be built. Scott says the federal government, working with the private sector, should take the lead on regulating AI. His campaign says he would support a moratorium on large data center construction while the state watches what Washington does, and Janoo backs one too, along with new taxes on digital advertising revenue and what her campaign calls the nation's strongest public standards for AI. Polls and campaign spending suggest this could be the closest governor's race in a decade.

Pro-Phil Scott super PAC launches ad blitz targeting Amanda Janoo

"National Republicans don’t spend almost half a million dollars to help keep a governor in office without a reason," per Vermont Public.

A Stronger Vermont, the Republican Governors Association's super PAC that spent $3 million to help elect Scott in 2016, spent nearly $175,000 late last week on TV and online ads painting Janoo as too far left, using a "magical thinking" line from her primary opponent Aly Richards, who has since criticized the RGA for misappropriating her quotes. Scott's campaign says the ads make fair points and that the RGA's help won't change his approach to the Trump administration. The latest Vermont Public poll put Scott's approval at 45%, down 15 points from 2022, and Janoo has outraised him $706,000 to $414,000.

Kismayo Kitchen Reopens in BTV on Riverside Ave — for Now

"Mohamed and Abdirisak both emphasized that they are actively seeking a new Chittenden County home for Kismayo Kitchen," per Seven Days.

The Somali American restaurant founded by the late Ahmed Omar reopened the weekend of Oct. 10 at 505 Riverside Ave., now run by his widow, Anisa Mohamed, with siblings Maryan and Abdirisak Maalin, keeping the mix of samosas, goat curry and Philly cheesesteaks with a slight price increase planned. The building qualified for a FEMA buyout and will eventually be torn down for green space, most likely in 2027, so they're hunting for a spot with at least 24 seats. It's open noon to 8 Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday, and 2:30 to 9:30 on Fridays.

Sober living home to open in Burlington to give men 'fresh start' at life

"This has saved my life on numerous occasions, and I'm hoping that even if I save one person's life, it means everything to me," per NBC5.

Fresh Start Recovery's Cedar Street house, also called Michael's Place in memory of Michael Prescott, who ran similar homes in Vermont and New York before his death in 2023, plans to open by the end of October. Eight men can live there at once for up to a year, five are already waiting to move in, and residents will get help finding jobs. The nonprofit still needs donations, from dishes to beds, and hopes to build a home for women next.

Previewing the Vermont International Film Festival in 48 Loglines

"Last year, attendance at the annual Vermont International Film Festival hit a 13-year high, according to executive director Steve MacQueen," per Seven Days.

The 10 day festival opens today at Main Street Landing Performing Arts Center and runs through Oct. 25, with 48 features, several shorts programs and six classics from 1976. Seven Days sums up every feature in a line, from Palme d'Or winner Fjord and Hirokazu Kore-eda's Look Back to The Last Critic, a Robert Christgau documentary featuring Winooski's Autumn Records. Tickets run $6 to $12, or $150 for a festival pass.

New café offers space for both caregivers and kids to play

"I’m just really excited to see kids in here using it and having fun and that’ll just make all my dreams come true right there," per Shelburne News.

Rachel and Andy Cartwright open Natural Nest Play Café at 2800 Shelburne Road on Monday, a Montessori style play space with toys made of natural, nontoxic materials for kids up to age 8, where caregivers supervise while they chat, drink coffee or get work done. Rachel says she's the first franchisee of the Delaware based business outside Delaware, and the building also has coworking space, private party rooms and a retail section. It holds 22 kids and their caregivers for now, with room to grow once Shelburne finishes its wastewater upgrade.

Essex Community Players Rebound From ‘Rocky Horror’ Drama

"Roya and I were both saying we feel like we’ve come home," per Seven Days.

The all volunteer company canceled The Rocky Horror Show this spring after crew members received anonymous threats, a $5,800 hit that came as four of its nine board members resigned, and in August Essex Police said the threats came from the show's own music director. New board president Beth Wilbur sees a bright future, and the board says it will read licensing contracts carefully and monitor its shows more closely, though some former members, including 15 year veteran Thalie Stapleton, aren't convinced. The season opens tonight at Memorial Hall in Essex with Crime and Punishment, A Comedy, five actors playing 50 characters through Oct. 31 ($21 to $25).

QUICK HITS

Offer extended to finalist in Burlington police chief search — Burlington has made an offer to a finalist for permanent police chief, pending a background check and the state's required polygraph, and Mayor Emma Mulvaney-Stanak is aiming for City Council confirmation at the Nov. 9 meeting. Interim Chief Shawn Burke has led the department since former Chief Jon Murad retired.

Despite federal drama, mail-in voting proceeding as planned — Vermonters are receiving and returning mail-in ballots after the Supreme Court blocked President Trump's executive order on Sept. 14 and declined to let the Postal Service rule take effect for this year's election. State elections director Sean Sheehan says anyone who hasn't received a ballot by mid-October should check the Vermont Voter Portal or contact their clerk.

Bystanders rescue driver after camper van rolls into Lake Champlain — Bystanders jumped into Lake Champlain Monday morning to help a Quebec man out of his camper van after it slid backward down the boat launch at the Coast Guard station, apparently pulled in by the weight of a boat being loaded or unloaded. Burlington Fire and the Coast Guard pulled the van out of the water.

New life jacket law arrives just as the cold-water season starts — A new state law requires anyone on the open deck of a boat underway on Vermont waters to wear a Coast Guard approved life jacket from Nov. 1 through May 1 each year. It covers kayaks, canoes and paddleboards along with motorboats, sailboats and pontoons, and exempts Coast Guard inspected commercial vessels.

12-year-old rescued after becoming separated from family on Camel’s Hump — A 12 year old from Boston who got separated from her family hiking Camel's Hump last Saturday evening was found unhurt after about an hour, with 17 rescuers responding to the Waterbury Backcountry Rescue Team's search. Crews say to pack a flashlight or headlamp for hiking in the dark and stay with your group.

UVM Athletics: Men's Hockey Opens the Gut Against No. 11 BU as Women's Hockey Visits Cornell

Men's hockey hosts No. 11 Boston University on Friday at 7 in its Hockey East opener and the TD Home Opener, and the first 500 fans get a cobranded TD/UVM T-shirt. The teams meet again Saturday at 7, with both games on ESPN+ and on WVMT with Owen Gund. The Terriers were picked third in the Hockey East preseason poll and lead the NCAA with 18 NHL Draft picks on the roster, headlined by Caleb Malhotra, the third overall pick in the 2026 draft. Vermont is 25-66-10 all time against BU, though Thomas Sinclair scored with 21.2 seconds left to win the last regular season meeting 3-2 at Agganis Arena in December, snapping a streak of 11 straight BU wins.

No. 16 men's soccer (8-1-3) hosts New Hampshire on Saturday at 1 at Virtue Field for the Rally Against Cancer game presented by Mascoma Bank, with a free lavender beanie for fans and the game on ESPN+. Vermont carries a 26 game regular season home unbeaten streak (18-0-8) that dates back to October 2023, and head coach Adrian Dubois faces his alma mater for the first time since taking over the program. The Wildcats (5-4-3) are still looking for their first America East win, and Vermont beat them 2-1 in overtime in last season's America East semifinals. Niklas Herceg's eight shutouts are tied for first in the country.

Women's hockey (3-1-0) is No. 15 in the USCHO poll for a second straight week and visits No. 14 Cornell on Friday at 6 and Saturday at 3, both on ESPN+. Vermont has scored first in all four games, is nine for nine on the penalty kill, and has yet to trail in regulation. Kaylee Lewis and Linnéa Misner share the team lead with four points, and Hilary Wilkin leads with two goals. The Cats are 2-12-1 all time against the Big Red, who haven't played yet this season, and last season's 4-3 win at Gutterson was only Vermont's second ever in the series. The next home series is the Pack the Gut Challenge against Northeastern on November 6.

Field hockey (10-2) plays at UAlbany on Friday at 12:30 on AmericaEast.TV, riding a three game winning streak against the team picked to tie Vermont for first in the America East preseason poll. Ila Gunner was named America East Goalkeeper of the Week after making five saves in last weekend's two wins, and Vermont leads the nation at 0.58 shutouts per game. No. 13 Yale comes to Moulton Winder Field on Sunday at noon for Rally Against Cancer, with the same free lavender beanies, and Senior Day against Bryant is next Friday at 3.

Women's soccer (4-4-5, 2-0-2 America East) plays at NJIT on Sunday at 2 on ESPN+, then hosts UAlbany next Thursday at 6 for its own Rally Against Cancer night. Cross country hosts the Fall Foliage Invite at Hard'ack in St. Albans on Sunday, women at 12:30 and men at 1:15, ahead of the America East Championship in Albany on October 30. Swimming and diving (1-0) visits New Hampshire on Saturday at 11. Men's basketball hosts Holy Cross in an exhibition at Patrick Gym on Saturday at 4 and Stonehill next Saturday at 2, and the women host a Saint Michael's exhibition on October 28.

Weather & Monday Update:

If anything outdoors is on your list this week, Monday and Thursday are the days to do it. Monday stays mostly dry and gray once the early showers wrap up, with a high around 65 and maybe a stray shower this evening before rain moves in overnight. Tuesday is the washout, with steady rain, south wind gusting to 30 and a chance of afternoon thunderstorms, adding up to around an inch by Wednesday morning while highs stay in the 50s. Wednesday opens with a leftover shower and stays cloudy and cool. Thursday brings the sun back, dry and chilly with a north breeze and a high near 55. Another round of rain arrives Friday, and the weekend brings the coldest air of the season so far, with Saturday stuck in the mid 40s and a few snowflakes possibly mixing in. Track it all week, with patio, swim, and sunset scores, at Burlington Right Now.

Monday's lineup is all evening. The Forever 38 crew takes a table at Trivia Mondays at Black Flannel [MEETUP] in Essex Junction at 6, and at 6:30 the monthly Collage Collective gathers at Expressive Arts Burlington on Flynn Avenue to cut, paste and create, by donation, with beginners welcome. Also at 6:30, Laura McPeake leads a drop in meditation class [MEETUP] at the Friends Meeting House on North Prospect Street, with simple guided meditations aimed at quieting busy thoughts. Violinist L. Shankar, one of the pioneers of East West music, who has played with Frank Zappa and Peter Gabriel, brings his 10 string double violin to the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge with doors at 7. Out in Shelburne, Chest Fever, billed as the official revival of The Band, performs The Last Waltz among the vines at Shelburne Vineyard from 7 to 10, rain or shine.

Tuesday's rain makes it a day for indoor plans. From noon to 5, the Colchester-Milton Rotary hosts a Red Cross blood drive at Our Lady of Grace in Colchester, with homemade baked goods after and a $15 e-gift card for every donor (book with the code CMROTARY). At 5, Fletcher Free Library hosts Writing for Healing, an hour of meditation, writing and Gateless feedback with snacks provided, and the Chamber & Economic Development of the Rutland Region brings its October mixer to Allen Pools & Spas in Williston from 5 to 7, benefiting Making Strides Against Breast Cancer. The Vermont Figure Drawing Collective draws from rotating models at Karma Bird House from 6 to 8, all skill levels welcome and no tickets needed. At 7, Dad Guild runs its open gym basketball at the Mater Christi School gym, Denver bluegrass quartet Magoo, whose debut album features Sam Bush on fiddle, plays the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge with doors at 7, NYU sociologist Lisa M. Stulberg talks with performer Kat Redniss about her book How to Win a Culture War at Phoenix Books, free with RSVP, and Kyle Stevens and Joe Friday play the Monkey House in Winooski with no cover. Queen City Brewery posted a Knot Knite for Tuesday too, so come do stuff with yarn. Partizanfilm screens Dead Media at 8:20, Joseph Scrimshaw's horror comedy about a haunted DVD and a movie night that won't die, and Jon McBride's Big Easy Tuesdays brings free jazz to The 126 at 9.

Wednesday is our first week of Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] indoors at UVM's Gutterson Fieldhouse, from 5:30 to 7:30, with a $12 day pass at the Campus Rec front desk in the Gucciardi Fitness Center, so come get some runs in. Earlier in the day, voters can meet outside City Hall on Church Street between 9:30 and 11 to drop off their ballots together, and Vermont Womenpreneurs gathers women business owners at Deep City for its monthly Biz Buzz at 9:45. Martin and Chris Kratt bring Wild Kratts Live 2.0 to the Flynn at 3:30 and 6:30, and seats are limited. At 5, wildcrafter and folk herbalist Broni Grala leads a Farm to Medicine Cabinet herb walk through medicinal plants at Shelburne Farms, Vermont Cider Lab in Essex Junction hosts a dog friendly Yappy Hour for VEG Cares with live music from 6, and Doma Bar on Pine Street gets its weekly All-Inclusive Dyke-Tacular going, an LGBTQ+ listening party with dancing. Runners can head out on an easy out and back 5K from 1st Republic [MEETUP] in Essex Junction at 5:30.

Wednesday evening keeps going. At 6, Lama Rod Owens gives a public Dharma talk and meditation at the O.N.E. Community Center, the Boardroom hosts cribbage [MEETUP] for all experience levels, and Mesmer Kava's BYO Book Club has no assigned reading, just bring whatever you're into. At 6:30 the Architecture + Design Film Series screens Good Work: Masters of the Building Arts at Contois Auditorium, and the Ward 1 NPA at the Friends Meeting House hears from Burlington Parks on the city's new Open Space Plan before a Q&A with Chittenden-15 House candidates Ben Bosley, Brian Cina and Troy Headrick. At 7, punk band Prince Daddy & The Hyena plays the Higher Ground Showcase Lounge, Chuck Wendig and Delilah Dawson talk about their new books The Calamities and Monstera at Phoenix Books, and the Queen City Ghostwalk's waterfront tour leaves from Union Station. UVM Theatre opens Annie Baker's The Aliens at the Royall Tyler Theatre at 7:30, with performances through Sunday, Partizanfilm shows the 1978 Invasion of the Body Snatchers at 8 before it closes for HVAC work from Oct. 16 through Oct. 29, and Hotel Vermont's weekly Jazz Night with Ray Vega runs from 8:30 to 10:30.

Thursday we're teaming up with South Burlington Rec's Social Pulse group for Ali T Live at J Ski's [MEETUP], a free indoor show from 7 to 9 at J Ski's on Main Street with free snacks and pizza while they last and a cash bar, so come hang out with us. The day starts at 7:30 AM with Braver Angels ambassador Mary K. Dennison on courageous citizenship at a Rotary club meeting at 185 Market Street in South Burlington, and the VermontBiz2Biz Expo at the DoubleTree opens its exhibit hall to the public from 8:30 to 3, alongside a Senator Welch business breakfast and the Vermont Business Growth Awards luncheon. At 5, YOURstory gathers women in midlife for a free story circle at the South Burlington Public Library, with just 13 seats so reserve ahead, Out in the 802's LGBTQ+ happy hour [MEETUP] meets at Lincoln's, the speakeasy up the alley by Red Square, and Adventure Dinner throws a free Pumpkin Fest pop-up at its Clubhouse on the edge of Winooski and Colchester until 9, costumes encouraged. The Flynn's Art of Community Storytelling workshop starts at 6 with no writing experience needed, and at 6:30 New York standup Kendall Farrell, a former Vermont's Funniest Comedian winner, plays the Vermont Comedy Club while UVM's Luis Vivanco tells the story of When the Bicycle Came to Vermont at Fletcher Free Library, free with RSVP. Déjà Rêvé Actors Guild opens the second weekend of Venus in Fur at Off Center at 7 with a cast and crew talkback after, Don Mahogany hosts Third Thursday Trivia at Butter Bar at 7, and the Buena Vista Orchestra, with players from the Buena Vista Social Club and AfroCuban All Stars, takes the Higher Ground Ballroom stage at 8.

Local News (All Links Clickable)

Sugar House Hotel in Winooski to Open Restaurant and Café-Bar

"Creemees are among many Vermont touches at the new hotel, which boasts light fixtures by Burlington’s AO Glass, locally crafted woodwork, rooms named for real sugarhouses around the state and the Nedde family’s own syrup in bottles behind the registration desk," per Seven Days.

The 115 room Sugar House Hotel opens Oct. 21 at 111 Winooski Falls Way, and both of its places to eat and drink are open to the public. In the lobby, Moss Café + Bar does espresso, pastries and grab and go sandwiches and salads by day, then wine, beer and cocktails with small bites at night, while the 75 seat Treetops restaurant on the eighth floor serves breakfast and dinner, with 40 outdoor seats looking out over the 100 acre nature preserve along the Winooski River. Food and beverage director Jacob Ennis came over from Warren's Pitcher Inn and hired executive chef Steve Zeno, formerly of Montpelier's Capitol Plaza Hotel, and sous chef Sean Richards, who owned Burlington's Queen City Café. The menus lean classic and local, from maple granola with Larson Farm yogurt at breakfast to a cider brined pork chop at dinner, and guests get a complimentary maple creemee when they arrive.

Construction begins on new affordable housing in Burlington

"This is a wealth-building tool for generations, not just for the first family, but for every family after," per WCAX.

Champlain Housing Trust broke ground Friday on the Shale Beach Condominiums, 30 permanently affordable homes in the Cambrian Rise neighborhood of the New North End, with the two and three bedroom units expected to sell for $175,000 to $210,000. Under the trust's shared equity model, buyers purchase the home while the trust keeps the land, and when they sell they split the appreciation with the trust so the home stays affordable for the next buyer. The condos sit next to 100 Cambrian Way, another permanently affordable building that welcomes its first residents next month.

Vermont governor’s race will test voters’ appetite for raising new taxes — or cutting them

"I think there is consensus that affordability is a problem. And healthcare is a major part of that. But the approach of how to get out of that is unclear," per VTDigger.

Democratic nominee Amanda Janoo, an economist from Burlington, wants a 2% surcharge on personal income over $250,000 and an 8% surcharge on income over $500,000, which Fair Share for Vermont estimates would raise $344 million a year, with the money going toward free primary and preventive care for every Vermonter. She also wants higher taxes on luxury second homes, commercial vacation rentals and corporate owned housing, plus a tax on big tech companies' digital ad revenue. Gov. Phil Scott, running for a sixth term, is pitching nearly the opposite, a still unspecified package of tax cuts or credits, and he has already told state agencies to plan budgets around less revenue. Scott argues a surtax would drive wealthy residents and businesses out of Vermont, though a Tax Policy Center fellow told VTDigger there is little evidence of significant "tax flight" elsewhere, and 57% of respondents in a recent Vermont Public poll backed a yearly tax on second homes.

General election ballots mailed out to Vermont voters

"Voters who want to return their ballots by mail need to fill them out and get them in the mail by Oct. 20," per WCAX.

You can also drop your ballot at your town clerk's office during business hours, or in an official drop box any time before Election Day on Nov. 3. Voting in person still works too, either with your mailed ballot or with a new one at the polls, and anyone who hasn't received a ballot by mid October should contact their town clerk.

Bernie Sanders Endorses Janoo for Vermont Governor

"I believe it’s time for a change, time for new leadership, time for a kind of energy and bold ideas that we’re not seeing in Montpelier right now," per Seven Days.

Sen. Bernie Sanders endorsed Amanda Janoo for governor on Wednesday in a video statement, saying he personally likes Gov. Phil Scott but backs Janoo's plans for free primary and preventive care, lower property taxes paid for by luxury second homes and large corporate investors, and a statewide moratorium on AI data centers. Janoo said the two met about two weeks earlier for a "great, nerdy policy conversation," and she already had Sen. Peter Welch, Rep. Becca Balint and former Gov. Howard Dean in her corner. Sanders has backed the Democrat in three of Scott's five previous races for governor. The polls disagree on where things stand, with UNH's Green Mountain State Poll showing Janoo up six points and a Vermont Public poll a few days later giving Scott a 10 point lead among likely voters. Should be quite the ending!

Vermont Legal Aid program to fight eviction may end due to lost funding

"We have many elders who are housing insecure and are facing homelessness," per WCAX.

Vermont Legal Aid's tenant representation pilot put a team of four attorneys on eviction cases starting in November 2024 and has opened and closed 207 cases, 54 of them for tenants over 60. It ends Oct. 31 because the state isn't replenishing the just over $1 million it got through Act 47, the Vermont Home Act of 2023. Legal Aid will keep offering free help, but project director Sara Kagle says less funding will make it harder to address Vermont's housing crisis.

Benefit concert brings Make-A-Wish families and jam band fans together in South Burlington

"It's a hometown show and there's nothing like a hometown show," per NBC5.

The Wish Benefit Tour's sold out stop at Higher Ground on Wednesday paired Dead & Company founding member Oteil Burbridge with Vermont groove trio LaMP, with all proceeds going to Make-A-Wish chapters in Vermont, Northeast New York, Massachusetts and Rhode Island. During the show, 19 year old wish alum Noah Cohen told Juniper, a 15 year old from Burlington who is battling leukemia, that her wish had been approved. She's headed on a musical tour of New York City in the spring, wrapping up with a recording session at Electric Lady Studios.

Gov. Scott swaps EV for hybrid, cites charging struggles

"I’ll continue to be an advocate for electric vehicles, carbonless and something I think most people would appreciate if we could charge them quicker and if they had a longer battery life. It just needs some more improvement," per WCAX.

Four years after becoming the first governor in the country to use an electric vehicle as his official state vehicle, Gov. Phil Scott disclosed last week that he gave up his Ford Lightning last fall, after putting about 70,000 miles on it, because charging stations were too hard to find on the road. He's driving a hybrid now and says he'll get another EV once the technology and the charging network improve.

Despite some overall progress, Vermont test scores show a widening achievement gap

"Our current funding system is not equitable, and it’s resulting in a widening between the haves and have nots," per VTDigger.

The state's first look at 2025-26 test results shows the proficiency gap between marginalized students and their peers now runs 30 to 38 percentage points, up from 26 to 36 last year, with the widest gap in sixth grade English language arts. The state counts students with disabilities, living in poverty, from racial or ethnic minorities and several other groups as marginalized, and they make up 57% of Vermont's roughly 80,000 students. There was some progress overall, as math proficiency in grades 3 through 9 rose 2.7 points and English rose 1.14, though only 41% of those students are proficient in math. Education Secretary Zoie Saunders says the gap makes the case for the foundation formula funding model the state is set to adopt in 2029, while advocates point to special education being siloed from general classrooms and to how schools respond to bias.

GlobalFoundries brings massive solar array, battery storage online in Essex Junction

"It’s the largest battery ever installed in Vermont, right here behind our own meter," per WCAX.

GlobalFoundries switched on a new solar array and a 16 megawatt battery storage system at its Essex Junction campus last Monday, with the panels covering more than 30 acres of underused land that includes an old parking lot and a brownfield. The battery discharges over four hours to cut the plant's draw on the regional grid at peak times, and Gov. Phil Scott, on hand for the ceremony, said the savings matter for all ratepayers.

Emerald ash borer has arrived in Charlotte, found at Mt. Philo

"Property owners should not remove healthy ash trees solely because emerald ash borer has been detected nearby," per The Charlotte News.

The state's invasive species coordinator has confirmed the first emerald ash borer detection in Charlotte, at Mount Philo State Park. The beetle's larvae feed under ash bark and girdle the tree, and the most definitive sign is small, D shaped exit holes in the trunk, along with thinning leaves, vertical bark splits and extra woodpecker activity. Chemical treatment can be very effective on trees with 30% or less crown loss, so the advice is to inspect your ash trees, call a certified arborist if you're concerned, and buy firewood locally and burn it where you bought it.

South Burlington couple loses home in fast-moving fire

"I heard what I thought was thumping upstairs. I thought it was an intruder. In fact, our house was on fire," per WCAX.

Stephen Snook and his wife were watching the Yankees game in the basement of their Butler Drive home last Wednesday night when the fire started, and within minutes flames were shooting out of the windows. They got out with their car, one cell phone and their lives. South Burlington's nearest crews were already on another call, so engines came from Burlington, Williston, the Vermont Air National Guard and UVM Rescue, and the cause is still unclear.

‘You can’t lose things like this’: Barre community rallies in attempt to save ice rink

"Once you shut down a building like this, it’s very, very hard to get it moving again," per Vermont Public.

About a week after Barre announced that the piping in its 52 year old BOR Arena was full of leaks and the rink likely wouldn't open this winter, local tradespeople started volunteering to try a fix. Heating installer Ed Patterson, whose son is a senior on the Spaulding High School hockey team, came up with a plan to reinforce the failed system with plastic tubing, and almost a dozen volunteers are working on it with equipment the city agreed to pay for. A patched section held pressure in its first test. The arena still needs a new roof and humidity control, which could mean a multimillion dollar bond vote in a city that still doesn't have a school budget.

Burlington seeks input on park playground renovations

"We’re really hoping specifically at Smalley that we’ll see a bit of a revitalized space back here by improving and renovating the playground," per WCAX.

Burlington Parks wants to give the playgrounds at Baird, Ethan Allen and Smalley parks the same accessible equipment Pomeroy Park got when it reopened in July, at around $200,000 per park, with help from the Parks Foundation's Playgrounds for All Forever campaign. Smalley's wooden play structures were removed in 2020 after they began to erode. The in person feedback session at Smalley was last Thursday, and the city also has an online survey covering all three parks.

Familiar faces from Norman Rockwell’s paintings visit Shelburne Museum

"He believed deeply that using real people was essential for making his pictures feel authentic," per The Charlotte News.

Norman Rockwell lived in Arlington for 14 years, creating more than 175 Saturday Evening Post covers there and famously paying his neighbors $5 and a cold Coca-Cola to model. Several of those models gathered at the Shelburne Museum on Sept. 26, including Mary Whalen, the grinning girl with the black eye in "The Young Lady with the Shiner," who remembered Rockwell getting down on his hands and knees to make her laugh. Don Trachte Jr. brought a list of the 211 people who modeled for Rockwell during his Arlington years. The museum's "Norman Rockwell: At Home in Vermont" exhibit is on view until Oct. 25, so there are two more weekends to catch it.

QUICK HITS

Repairs underway at downtown Burlington parking garages — The Downtown, Marketplace and Lakeview garages stay open during maintenance, but elevator access may be limited. The City Council approved a $1.6 million loan for the work last Monday, to be paid back with parking revenue.

Vermont hip hop band pens tune about online relationship — A2VT, named Best Hip Hop Group by Seven Days last year, released the single "Before The Night Is Over" in early October, with a video shot around downtown Burlington. The band has been making music in Vermont since 2012, after its members fled conflict in Burundi, Somalia and Tanzania.

State board approves landing strip at home of Beta CEO — A state transportation board gave Beta Technologies CEO Kyle Clark final approval last Thursday for a 900 foot landing strip at his home in Lincoln, with conditions limiting when he can fly in and out. The plan had divided the Addison County town and been fought in and out of court since 2022.

Boat sinks at Colchester marina, fuel spills into Lake Champlain — A boat sank at a marina along West Lakeshore Drive in Colchester on Sunday evening, spilling fuel into the lake. Colchester Fire and the state's hazmat team deployed containment booms, and the boat was set to be removed Monday.

UVM Athletics: McNabb Wins New Englands as Women's Hockey Sweeps Its First Road Trip

Zoey McNabb won the women's 5k at the New England Championships in Hopkinton, N.H., on Friday, finishing 17.2 seconds ahead of the next runner. She's the first Vermont winner there since Judi St. Hilaire in 1980 and only the second Catamount ever named New England Champion. The men took third with 87 points, just two behind winner Providence, for the program's first men's team trophy position since it won the whole thing in 1958, led by Will Locke in fifth at 24:58.60. The women placed fourth, with Isabella Fryer running her fastest 5k of the fall. UVM hosts the Fall Foliage Invite at Hard'ack in St. Albans on Sunday, women at 12:30 and men at 1:15, its final tune up before the America East Championship.

No. 15 women's hockey swept Franklin Pierce to start 3-1-0, its best start since 2022-23. Friday's 2-1 win came on Zoe Charland's first career goal and a Lauren O'Hara goal with 45 seconds left in the second, with Ellie Simmons making 18 saves in her first start of the season. Saturday's 4-0 win had 11 different players record a point, including Gracesyn Louis scoring her first career NCAA goal in her first regular season game, and Tara Bach stopped all 19 shots for her second shutout of the season. The Cats play at Cornell on Friday at 6 and Saturday at 3 on ESPN+.

Men's hockey dropped its opener 3-0 at Bentley on Friday. Vermont outshot the Falcons 8-0 over the opening nine minutes, but Bentley scored on two of its first four shots, Colin Kessler hit the post in the second, and Lukas Swedin made 16 saves over the final two periods for his third career shutout. Eight Catamounts made their debuts, and Cédrick Guindon led all skaters with five shots on goal. No. 14 Boston University comes to Gutterson on Friday and Saturday at 7 on ESPN+ and WVMT, and Friday is the TD Home Opener, with cobranded T-shirts for the first 500 fans.

Field hockey (10-2) has won three straight, all shutouts. Consu de Castro deflected in a Veerle Nijhuis shot with 11 minutes left in the third quarter to beat UMass Lowell 1-0 on Friday for Vermont's first conference win, and on Sunday Emily Enden scored off a penalty corner 1:43 into overtime to beat Appalachian State 1-0, her first career game winner. That's double digit wins for the fifth time in six seasons. The Cats play at UAlbany on Friday, then host Yale on Sunday at noon for Rally Against Cancer presented by Mascoma Bank.

No. 16 men's soccer won 1-0 at UMBC on Saturday when Luis Vetter headed in an Aleksei Carnier cross in the 87th minute, its first win at UMBC since 2018. Niklas Herceg posted his eighth shutout of the season and 24th of his career, and the Cats (8-1-3) remain unbeaten in conference play. They host New Hampshire on Saturday at 1 at Virtue Field, with a free lavender beanie for fans for Rally Against Cancer. Women's soccer played to a 0-0 draw at Bryant on Sunday, putting seven shots on goal to Bryant's zero as Sophia Kling kept her third clean sheet, and plays at NJIT on Sunday at 2. Men's basketball tips off with a Holy Cross exhibition at Patrick Gym on Saturday at 4.

Podcast Picks of the Week:

Sometimes you don’t want to read, you want to listen (or watch). Check out this week’s podcast picks:

Vermont Talks sat down at Brio Coffeeworks on Pine Street with Darius and Taylor of the Burlington Night Council, the crew behind Wizard Night and the other costumed bar crawls that keep turning up on Church Street and on r/burlington. Clown Night is when it broke containment, with 30 to 40 clowns downtown and a pile of Reddit posts, and their apology to anyone who got spooked was "maybe only a little sorry." The costumes are cheap on purpose. A wizard hat is cardboard, duct tape and the cheapest acrylic paint you can find, plus a bathrobe, because their motto is "the crawl is for all." They do it downtown instead of at a house party because they want to use the city's shared public spaces, and they pick bars with no cover so people who aren't drinking don't pay $10 to stand there. The rules are "have fun, be nice, tip well," and if your costume calls for a weapon, bring a banana instead of a toy gun. To find the next one, watch for posters, since the crew gathers on the Three Needs patio around 9, and they're teasing a Wrestling Night and a Ghost Night. Go ahead and check out the 30 minute listen. 

Second podcast pick this week:

Vermont Edition spent part of its September 10th hour with Seven Days music editor Chris Farnsworth on what the Radio Bean meant to Burlington, two days after it closed. Lee Anderson saw an empty storefront on North Winooski Avenue in December 2000 and started maxing out credit cards to open it. Farnsworth called the closing "pure insurance," where Nectar's and Metronome were more about rent. What made the room special was that nobody ever asked a band for its social media numbers before booking it, and Robber Robber, Lily Seabird and Greg Freeman all got their start there. Some incredible moments include birthday parties that ran from 8 AM to 2 AM, a packed and loud room going quiet as a movie theater for Michael Chorney's band, and the send off, a Brass Balagan funeral procession to Church Street that Grace Potter joined. Farnsworth says the Lee Anderson era is done, but a version of the Bean could come back. The rest of the hour is novelist Daniel Mason on Country People, his comic novel about a California family that moves to southern Vermont, where the most autobiographical character is the dog.

Local Podcast Roundup

Four weeks of Vermont podcasts this time, so here's the full catch up. The Vermont Conversation had Attorney General Charity Clark on suing Trump and winning $92.7 million from Meta, filmmaker Bess O'Brien on her documentary Every Day: Big and Small, Hisham Awartani the week a jury convicted Jason Eaton in the North Prospect Street shooting, and novelist Richard North Patterson on his book Tripwires. 802 News with Mark Johnson also sat down with Bess O'Brien, calling the film her love story to Vermont, and Vermont Talks, besides the Night Council, recorded at Uncommon Coffee in Essex with Mima Tipper, author of Channeling Marilyn.

Vermont Edition ran fifteen episodes in the window. Three of the clergy arrested at the Williston ICE facility talked about the protest and their faith, Carhartt's archivist explained when farm clothes became high fashion, and Adjutant General Hank Harder talked about the 158th Fighter Wing coming home from deployment. There was a Hispanic Heritage Month hour with DJ Adru's new Sunday radio show, an hour on mushroom hunting, the annual fall gardening show with Charlie Nardozzi, the Bennington Museum's Vermont Vice exhibit with Thea Lewis's new book, the Town by Town series in Lemington, the making of Vermont Public's 2026 election poll, and interviews with the candidates for Attorney General and Secretary of State. The Frequency followed the Eaton trial from opening day to the guilty verdict, along with UVM Health cutting about 200 jobs, a new Spanish language radio hour, flood buyout money finally coming through, a promising leaf peeping season, the push to keep buses rolling, the Attorney General charging ICE protesters, the poll showing a tight governor's race, what Vermonters think about taxing second homes, data centers, help for nesting turtles, and why home heating fuel costs more this season. Vermont This Week covered the Brattleboro birthing center reversal, the UVM Health and Dartmouth Health layoffs, the protester charges and the Eaton verdict, and the new poll. Brave Little State asked whether private equity is taking over Vermont's veterinary market, and But Why hit its 300th episode and then explained growing pains.

Over on The Morning Drive, Cathy Davis explained the Lake Champlain Chamber's new Downtown Business Alliance, Drive Electric Vermont talked EV programs, Mark Redmond of Spectrum previewed the Empty Bowl dinner, and Governor Phil Scott, Amanda Janoo, Molly Gray and a long line of legislative candidates came through the studio, while Vermont Viewpoint on WDEV ran its own daily lineup of candidates. There's No "A" in Creemee opened its third season with bears and candidate poetry, then had Lieutenant Governor John Rodgers and weird campaign foods, and Charity Clark on the Williston ICE protester arrests. Net Zero Energy, Burlington Electric's own show, talked with NESEA about why the new all electric Burlington High School matters. VCET's Start Here had Rachael Floreani of Burlington Bio on turning discarded food into affordable food and Omari Bouknight of Resonant Link Medical on wireless charging for medical implants. Rumble Strip told the story of Montpelier best friends Rob Mermin and Bill Morancy in The Last Chapter. Happy Vermont visited Main Street in Jamaica and the stone chapel behind the von Trapp Family Lodge, Abstract VT posted three live sets recorded at the Venetian Soda Lounge, and The Octagon opened its third season with a 2026 ski and gear review.
